specification_purpose: Authorize at most one logical confirmatory evaluation of the 4 published candidates on the v3 confirmatory window, and record the scope, the window, the data boundary, the window-benchmark rule, the output layout, the code identity, the single decision criterion, the attempt budget, the preconditions, the stopping conditions, the falsifiers and the rollback. No evaluation may run before the window exists.

scope.data_scope_rule: the data scope is the 4 in-scope assets plus the window benchmark series; the benchmark is retrieved with the window, hash-verified and aligned with the asset series, and it is counted as an exposed asset like every other

code_identity.note: The identity of a confirmatory run is the composite of the canonical digest of the hashed v1 engine and the canonical digest of the confirmatory execution path. The checkout-dependent ordered digest compute_code_hash() is an environment fact and is never used as an identity.

window.evaluation_window_rule: The evaluated window is exactly the first minimum_closed_hourly_candles closed hourly candles at or after the window start, so it ends at the earliest instant the frozen boundary allows. The evaluated window's length does not depend on when the run happens, and the window may not be extended, shortened or re-based at run time.

data_boundary.readiness_test: a bounded metadata-only probe of the provider's server time and the spot exchange status of the in-scope pairs and of the benchmark pair; it fetches no candle and does not increment holdout_exposed_count

benchmark_rule.alignment_rule: Align BTC and target asset by UTC candle close; no forward fill for missing BTC observations
fail_closed: the benchmark series is shorter than the evaluated window
the benchmark series is not index-aligned with the asset series
benchmark_rule.note: The window benchmark series is retrieved with the window, hash-verified like every other window dataset and aligned with the asset series by UTC candle close before the engine is called. A missing, a short or a misaligned benchmark aborts the run; the published development benchmark may not be substituted for it.

decision_rule.note: The v3 line states exactly one confirmatory criterion. The v2 line had to amend two frozen artifacts that disagreed about it; the v3 protocol and this authorization state one criterion and the execution path applies no second one.

preconditions: the authorization and the confirmatory protocol are committed
the metadata-only readiness test has passed and its record is in the window manifest
holdout_exposed_count is 0, or the run is a resume of the same exposure event
the live code identity equals the recorded code identity
the evaluation scope equals the frozen selected-configurations manifest
the window benchmark series is retrievable, hash-verifiable and index-aligned with the asset series
the v1 artifacts, the v2 selection outputs and the v3 selection outputs are byte-unchanged
stopping_conditions: the run stops when every in-scope asset has been evaluated
the run stops at the first boundary violation, rolls back and releases the attempt
the run stops when the window is spent: a second read of the window is refused
the run stops before the engine is called when the window benchmark is missing, short or misaligned
an inconclusive outcome is reported, never hidden
if no configuration survives the preregistered promotion rule, that null result is reported
falsifiers: the evaluated parameters differ from the frozen candidate manifest entry
the grid is extended, re-ranked or re-tuned on the window
a candle inside the window is read more than once
holdout_exposed_count is incremented outside a confirmatory read
the v1 holdout is re-opened, or the v2 confirmatory window or the v2 and v3 selection outputs are tallied with
an asset of the frozen scope is omitted from the report
the window benchmark series is missing, short or misaligned and the evaluation proceeds anyway
the published development benchmark is substituted for the window benchmark
a second confirmatory decision criterion is applied

rollback.before_the_first_payload_read: an abort rolls back every artifact the run created and leaves holdout_exposed_count = 0, so the attempt is released
rollback.after_a_payload_read: an abort leaves the exposure in place: the run is recorded as EXPOSED_ABORTED, the window is spent, and the report must state that the window was consumed without a completed evaluation
rollback.resume: an interrupted run is resumed from the verified shards and the already retrieved, hash-verified datasets; the number of resumes is bounded by max_retries_on_technical_failure

deviation_disclosure.scope: the completed v1 and v2 runs
deviation_disclosure.statement: The completed v1 and v2 runs evaluated the BTC trend filter against a BTC EMA taken from a different period; the deviation is a disclosure for the final report and is not repaired here.
deviation_disclosure.v3_run_alignment: the v3 run evaluated the BTC trend filter against the index-aligned v3 benchmark dataset

supersedes.reason: The interim draft of this artifact was an unverified adaptation of the v2 authorization: it named the v2 confirmatory window, the v2 output paths and the v2 data manifest. It was never verified and never committed. This artifact supersedes it and is the versioned, hash-bound authorization of the v3 confirmatory evaluation.

durability.rule: The authorization takes effect when this artifact is committed. No confirmatory-window candle may be read and no evaluation may run before the commit that carries this artifact exists.
durability.note: The commit hash is recorded by the committing session. This artifact is not rewritten after that commit, because its manifest_hash must not change.

hashing.note: manifest_hash is the sha256 of the document body with manifest_hash removed, so the document does not hash itself into a cycle.
